reviews.review: Not a bad game. Judged a bit too harshly. If you look at it as if it is "Skyrim in space", instead of Mass Effect 4, you'll have a better time. The combat is pretty decent. The graphics look good. One issue is that there are almost too many quests, perhaps that's why the quality can waver on some missions. Anyway, I give it 8/10 if you consider it on it's own without comparing it to Mass Effect.

i will eb one of those that is bit neutral. Story is decetn I would say. I like the fact unlike the trilogy we are really a rookie, at being in charge, being a leader, exploring. It gives a fresh new take to the ME world. That being said still see certain bugs. Like when talking to squadmates Ryder's hands go trhough each other and the upgrade menu is less simple to understand compared to the trilogy.

I recommend it - took some heat on release but all in all its a good game, especially if you like Bioware games. It doesn't really hold up to the original trilogy story wise, but as a stand alone game it provided plenty of entertainment, with the classic Bioware charm (except for the plastic faces of course, but lets be real the original trilogy was not any better in that regard).

Now the ugly;
The characters (at least at the start) did not feel as well fleshed out or engaging as the ME1-3 ones, I found it hard to care for any of them, but especially Liam and Cora. Even by end of game, still could not care less what happened to those two, but Drack, Peebee and Jaal were very fun to have around. 

I think the biggest sin of this game is the ending. [spoiler] While the mission itself was grand, and visually nice, there was absolutely 0 urgency to the whole thing. In previous Mass Effect games, the last missions had a lot of weight, you made decisions that could cost you your crew. In this, you just kind of land, kick ass, and leave. It left me wondering whether there was more story if I complete some side missions or something, but then had to look it up to confirm that was the ending. Seriously? Also what even happened to that remnant AI that I had placed with SAM? At one point it just... disappeared and was never mentioned again lol [/spoiler]

As regards the systems in the game (crafting, the profiles etc) I can't really complain - I completed the game with only crafting the essential items (and the remnant armour set), never touched the profiles, and auto assigned levels on secondary characters. I like that the game doesn't force you to use all the systems they have in place, but that's about it.

I bought and played this game many years after it came out. That being said, I went in knowing that MEA got a lot of heat back in 2017. Yes, this game is not up to standard when compared with the original trilogy, however, MEA is well written and does have it moments of shine. Gameplay is good, the scenery is beautiful and most of the secondary characters were well implemented. At the end, it felt that, if EA had put another year in development time, the first reviews would've been much better. The worst part of this journey is having to commit to EA's launcher, but once you accept that, it is a story you'll enjoy playing through.

PS: MEA does deserve a sequel
